discoveries: Repository collects public client audit reports; each report is scoped to specific commit/program/version.
An audit report is historical evidence and does not certify later deployed code or operational configuration.
No report was selected as a direct audit of SYLPH in this review.
patterns: bind security claims to audited commit and scope
map findings to current code revision
retest fixes and regressions independently
sources.overlap: Useful for external program/protocol security references but no direct report-level integration identified.
risks: stale findings or unaudited new code
validation: identify exact report and target commit
verify current deployed program hash
do not treat report as blanket safety claim

provenance: Official Shopify Toxiproxy README and project description
discoveries: Toxiproxy is a TCP proxy for simulating network/system conditions in resilience tests.
It can support deterministic latency, timeout and connection fault injection for stream/RPC adapters.
It does not model all gRPC/QUIC/UDP protocol behaviors and would require an isolated test network.
patterns: inject bounded latency and disconnect faults
replay deterministic failure schedules
assert recovery and no silent data loss
sources.overlap: Existing unit tests mock failures; a proxy could add integration-level TCP failure testing without replacing code.
risks: test proxy configuration can expose services
chaos can disturb shared user services if misconfigured
validation: use isolated test ports/processes
test recovery under timeout/reset/rate-limit cases
never point fault injection at production endpoints

provenance: Official Syndica Sig README and repository metadata
discoveries: Sig is a Solana validator client implementation written in Zig.
A distinct client implementation can serve protocol differential testing but is not automatically independent market evidence.
Running a validator client requires significant infrastructure and version tracking.
patterns: compare client behavior on fixed block/transaction vectors
record client version and feature activation
treat divergence as a signal for investigation, not immediate truth selection
sources.overlap: Potential client diversity source; not a direct data adapter for current application.
risks: different client outputs around edge cases
validation: pin release and feature set
compare against Agave/Firedancer vectors
do not use an unverified client as sole canonical source

provenance: Official Sombra README and repository description
discoveries: Sombra describes a Solana pre-transaction risk/evidence console for wallets, signatures, blocks and programs.
A pre-transaction screen is a derived risk signal and cannot guarantee post-submit execution or prevent all malicious token behavior.
No SYLPH integration or provider authority was verified.
patterns: show supporting evidence with each risk result
fail closed when required evidence is unavailable
separate advisory risk from signing authorization
sources.overlap: Potentially overlaps RugCheck/GoPlus and existing manual research surface; needs source-by-source comparison.
validation: inspect code, data provenance and license
test exact mint/transaction binding
ensure advisory output cannot authorize execution

provenance: Official OpenSol Agent README and repository description
discoveries: Project describes a CLI-first Solana intelligence agent producing wallet, token and transaction risk reports.
Agent-generated reports are derived outputs that need explicit source provenance and deterministic verification.
No credentials, tool access, or SYLPH integration were examined or configured.
patterns: use bounded read-only tools
cite source records in generated findings
keep AI summaries separate from canonical decisions
